messages:
talia-sales: Heads-up — Orpheus wants to validate Orpheus-30b-lite for a Dedicated POC. Needs: EU data residency, BYOK/HSM, audit logs, and an estimate for 4-bit quant cost. Asking for compatibility check + timeline. Model artifact: https://models.orpheus.ai/30b-lite.tar.gz. CC @noah-eng @anya-ml
noah-eng: Thanks. Quick checklist: tokenizer format? rotary embeddings? n_head? context length? Also license for transformations (quantize/tokenizer adapt)?
talia-sales: They've shared model manifest in the portal. Key bits: n_head=48, rotary=true, ctx=4096. License: permissive, but they want us to confirm we can run quantization and adapter work.
anya-ml: Orpheus-30b-lite uses a SentencePiece vocab (spm) with custom normalization rules. Our runtime supports spm but custom norms may require a small adapter to match token offsets. KV-cache looks standard but we should run an automatic inspect.
kevin-sre: BW-wise Dedicated can do EU-only placement. BYOK via external HSM is supported but requires HSM cert and network whitelisting. Will need legal + infra signoff. Also confirm SLA target — are they expecting sub-150ms p50?
talia-sales: They asked for 99.9 uptime and p50 <= 120ms for short prompts. They'll accept slightly higher for long contexts.
noah-eng: I'll run the inspector tomorrow morning. Command I'll use:
```
ri inspect model --source https://models.orpheus.ai/30b-lite.tar.gz --tokenizer --kv-layout --ops-report
```
If tokenizer norms differ we can add an adapter shim that normalizes inputs pre-tokenize. That usually takes a day to validate.
ci-bot: Inspect job queued (id=99221). Estimated runtime: 2h.
noah-eng: Inspect result: tokenizer: supported (spm) BUT normalization rules mismatch flagged (lowercase vs unicode_norm). KV-cache: ok. Ops-report: custom fused attention block present; runtime can fallback to reference kernel but will cost ~15% latency. Logs: https://redwood.internal/jobs/99221/logs
anya-ml: Fused attention fallback is fine for POC. For production we should test performance with our kernel devs. For quant: NF4 recommended for CPU-cost tradeoff; we'll run a 1k prompt sanity eval to measure quality drop. That takes ~24–48h including quant runs.
talia-sales: Pricing: can you ballpark token cost delta for 4-bit on Dedicated? They want budget for the POC.
noah-eng: rough math: baseline FP16 infer cost ~ $0.015 / 1k tokens. With 4-bit NF4 we estimate ~40–55% cost reduction → ~ $0.007–0.009 / 1k tokens, depending on batching. For Dedicated committed capacity we can offer a 20% discount off list. Precise estimate after quant run and batch tuning.
judy-secu: Security note: we require completed security questionnaire + signed DPA for EU residency. For BYOK/HSM we need their HSM vendor, certs, and a network plan. Also we need to add a clause allowing tokenization/quantization transforms in the contract if we perform them. I can draft the addendum.
kevin-sre: Timeline: if inspector ok (done), adapter small (1 day), quant eval (48h), legal + HSM onboarding (variable, assume 5–10 business days). For a minimal internal POC in EU env, optimistic ~10 business days; conservative 3 weeks.
noah-eng: Next steps: (1) confirm permission to transform artifacts (license ok per portal but want written consent), (2) request their spm & norm files, (3) approve HSM vendor + kick legal. I'll start a kernel perf ticket for fused-att fallback to quantify the 15% hit.
talia-sales: I'll ping Orpheus for explicit transform consent, upload their security questionnaire, and ask for HSM details. I'll also push the draft pricing note (use number range you gave).
anya-ml: After we get the tokenizer norm files I'll run a quick generation check (10 prompts) and then the 1k eval post-quant.
ci-bot: Inspect job 99221: COMPLETE. Artifacts: token-report.txt, kv-check.json, ops-report.html.
talia-sales: Thanks all — I'll update Orpheus and loop legal. Will post updates here. :rocket:
